data.narrative:
Electric Hydrogen, a Series C climate and energy company founded by Raffi Garabedian and David Eaglesham, commands a current post-money valuation of $1.0B following $700M in total capital raised. The valuation assessment draws from a comparable universe of 9 private and 1 public company (LNZA) operating in climate and energy infrastructure, including peers such as KoBold Metals, Amogy, Redwood Materials, and Helion.

Two triangulation methods apply to this stage and sector. Stage-progression analysis, applying a typical 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $1.0B last post-money round, implies a forward valuation of $1.7B. Peer-median analysis across three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables yields a $3.0B median, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy, Series C) to $6.0B (Redwood Materials, Series D). The peer set exhibits substantial dispersion, reflecting variation in technology maturity and capital intensity within the sector.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.4B (high), with a median of $2.3B. This implies potential appreciation of 40% to 240% from the current round. The wide spread reflects uncertainty in comparable company selection and stage-appropriate valuation multiples in an early-stage, capital-intensive sector. Execution risk on technology demonstration and commercialization timelines represents the primary sensitivity.
